findings.finding: Opens 'We did not replicate three of the four simulation headlines of Chen (2021), who reported biased direct-effect estimates, percentile bootstrap intervals that cover the true value far too rarely, and power for the mediated interaction (MINT) near zero.' Verdict, cited source and original findings in one sentence; composite verdict (3 of 4 not replicated, H4 'holds in part') matches packet statuses H1-H3 not_replicated, H4 partly_replicated.
Published-versus-ours numbers follow at once for every headline component: 85.42% vs 0.00%, 43.62 vs 0.04 points, 0.013 (raw 0.063) vs 0.802 (raw 0.852), H4 86.3%/89.2% with the both-zero exception.

Limit of evidence (Head Start restricted-use data; S9 holds in 10 of 15) and the unseeded bootstrap follow; tolerances and 'point estimates, not equivalence' stated. The limit comes after the four headline components rather than as sentence 2; acceptable for a four-part composite headline.

Repeats the verdict with Table 4.8/4.9/Figure 4.28 numbers for H1-H3, then the H4 partial result, then the limits (Head Start, unseeded bootstrap), then 'No estimate reverses its sign' and Monte Carlo errors (.007, .002, 0.005/0.019).
Tolerances restated; research questions follow the verdict, not precede it. First paragraph is long (polish).
Readable without the research conversation; 'Bradley's Type I range' and PNDE/TNDE are used on page 1 before definition (pages 3-4) -- polish.

Narrates that Python was chosen without first asking the project owner. This is a consequential software departure, so retaining it is defensible; the who-asked-whom detail is process narration (polish).
Only 'master' named; no commit hash or working branch anywhere (commit_refs.py accepted, no errors). Files are linked and commands given; stage_checks cues returned no flagged occurrences.

Recomputed from source-values/table_4_8.csv and table_4_9.csv (both checked against source PDF pp. 102 and 138): E1 mean(100 - within.10) over 6 PNDE/TNDE rows = 85.4167 -> 85.42; E2 95 - mean coverage = 43.619 -> 43.62; E3 mean(above - below) = 47.071 -> 47.07. Ours from results/table49_ours.csv: E2 0.0358 -> 0.04, E3 0.3258 -> 0.33; E1 0.00 from results/table48_ours.csv (all within .05).

results/digitized_rates.csv Figure 4.28, n = 500, a = .59, h = .34: cut2 .0683 (err .0052), cut3 .0571 (err .0131), cut1 occluded; mean .0627, excess .0127 -> 0.013; ours .9009/.8027 mean .8518 -> excess .802; all-cutoff .8361 = summary.json 'n=500 ah=0.2006'.
H4 shares 70.0/74.0/80.1/86.3/89.6% and 35.9/53.3/61.5/89.2/91.4%, cutoff ranges 85.7-87.0% and 88.3-89.9% match results/statement_checks.csv summary rows.

All 13 packet claims (H1-H4, S1-S9) appear with statuses matching the packet (not_replicated, partly_replicated, blocked, replicated, not_established). writer-manifest claim_map locations checked: e.g. S9 in abstract p.1, Section 1 p.2, 4.8 p.9, 6.10 p.16, Table 3 p.10.
Each claim has a row with precision, numerical and scope labels; S5 'all 48 reproduced' = 24 differences + 24 SBs (secondary/table_arithmetic.csv, all True).
S7 and S8 are discussed with their not-established reasons; S8 search terms recorded.
All seven packet limitations present in order and faithful; item 1 is more hedged than the packet ('evidently ... an inference from her figures'), which is appropriate.
Claim-specific limits (H3 reading error 0.0091 at cutoffs 2-3; H4 tentative; S1 zero-estimate pattern partial; S5 divisor intent unknown) retained.
Post-hoc choice of the E4 cell disclosed in body and in Table 1 caption on page 1.
Separates Chen's model, design, definitions and published numbers from our six contributions, each labeled (our simulation, our calculation with her code, our reading of her figures, etc.).

Exact R replay is limited explicitly: 'reproduces her printed pipeline, not her published runs'; 'It does not reproduce her bootstrap, which sets no seed.' Interval results are Python with our seeds and agree 'only in distribution'. Not overstated.
Each disagreement tests our-side explanations first and gives side and confidence matching DISAGREEMENTS.yaml.

Source identity verified against source/chen2021.pdf title page (Donna Chen, UNL, December 2021, advisers Bovaird & Wheeler; SHA-256 9206b3d8...e557, 6,720,692 bytes, 203 pages). Findings verified: p.147 'When bias was present, the measure of bias was a negative value'; p.150 'the true parameter value systematically fell above the CIs'; p.121 'All power for MINT is near zero'; p.148 'never reached the .80 level'; p.150 'Tentatively, a minimum sample size of 5000 has accurate Type I error rates and power above .80, regardless of cutoff score'.

S9 summary checked against p.143 ('if the RCT was significant, the RDD estimate would not be significant') and Table 4.7 intervals on PDF pp. 97-98; 10 of 15 opposite reproduced from results/significance_conclusions.json.

E1 tolerance 0.005 (mean of six 2-decimal values), E2 0.005, E3 0.01 (difference of two such means), E4 0.0091 measurement (mean of .0052 and .0131 = .00915, rounded down, declared not set in the plan). Labels recomputed: E1 smaller, zero vs nonzero (ours 0.00 within 0.005); E2/E3 smaller, same direction (0.04 > 0.005, 0.33 > 0.01); E4 larger, same (0.802 vs 0.0127, both beyond 0.0091); E5 not established. Caption carries 'Descriptive point estimates; not equivalence.'

Uncertainty separated from tolerance: MC SE .007 per rate, .002 for E4 (sqrt(.852*.148/32000) = .0020), E2/E3 means 0.005 (independent) or 0.019 (correlated) from results/mc_se_headline.json; recomputed approximately from binomial variance (0.0050, 0.0193). Paper says the E2/E3 sign agreement holds 'as point estimates', which is the right qualification since 0.04 is about 2 correlated SEs.

Published 'PNDE and TNDE within [-.10, .10] in only 12.50-18.75% of conditions, with negative bias' = Table 4.8 PNDE/TNDE rows 12.50-18.75 and p.147. Ours 'within [-.05, .05] in 100% ... largest |bias| 0.016' = table48_ours.csv (within_05 100, max 0.0155).
Published coverage 24.10-83.99%, above 14.08-75.55%, below 0.34-1.93% = Table 4.9. Ours coverage 94.59-95.63 -> '94.6-95.6', above 2.52-2.90, below 1.84-2.71 = table49_ours.csv.

Published 'near zero at every sample size; never reaches .80 (Figure 4.28: 0.057-0.068 in this cell)' = p.121, p.148 and digitized_rates.csv (.0571, .0683). Ours 0.852 (cutoffs 2-3), 0.836 (all), >= .97 for ah >= .13 from n = 1,000 (summary.json minimum 0.9735).

Published quotes p.150 recommendation incl. 'tentative'. Ours 86.3%/89.2%, 'similar at each cutoff' (85.7-87.0%, 88.3-89.9%), both-zero products conservative (.0015-.0020) = statement_checks.csv summary rows and disagreement_tests.json n5000.both_paths_zero. Not a placeholder.

H4 classified nonscalar with applicability text 'qualitative, no scalar contrast'; the source statement (p.150) is a qualitative design recommendation over the whole grid with no single signed contrast; magnitude and direction 'not established', tolerance 'not applicable', claim verdict 'partial' kept separate from the missing magnitude. No contrasts or components exist on the source claim, so none are omitted.
The shares behind the partial verdict are retained with per-cutoff ranges and exceptions; no pooled scalar margin invented.
